question.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y=0.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let $y={e}^{\lambda x}.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\lambda {e}^{\lambda x},\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}={\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}+4\lambda {e}^{\lambda x}+4{e}^{\lambda x} & =0 \\ {e}^{\lambda x}({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +4) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The auxiliary equation is therefore

$$
{\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +4=0.
$$

Factoring the auxiliary equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(\lambda +2)(\lambda +2)=0 \\ (\lambda +2)^{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\lambda =-2$ is a repeated root.

So the general solution to the differential equation is

$$
y=A{e}^{-2x}+Bx{e}^{-2x}.
$$
